item.text: {"question_id":"4B.10","answer":"The supplied evidence does not establish that, by the end of 2023, Félix Tshisekedi had left political freedom and democratic resilience durably stronger than inherited. There were some favorable institutional and procedural developments: five rights-related laws were enacted; UNDP-supported recruitment and training expanded the magistrate corps and selected justice access and case outputs; a mixed international expert team externally audited the electoral register and judged it reliable; the government permitted some domestic and international monitoring; the National Commission on Human Rights issued reports, visited detention centers, trained magistrates, and followed up complaints; Tshisekedi issued an anti-exclusion, anti-fraud, and electoral-protection directive; the government strengthened cooperation with the ICC; and at least one peaceful 2023 protest was escorted by police. [BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0011-E014, BATCH-0009-E001, BATCH-0019-E001, BATCH-0022-E014] These items show formal commitments, monitoring capacity, and selected outputs, but they do not demonstrate nationwide implementation, independent and effective review, correction of abuses, or durable effects. The audit was published by CENI and relied partly on its internal audit, while the government directive, presidential commitments, ICC agreement, and justice outputs lack evidence here of complete enforcement or remedy. [BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0009-E001, BATCH-0019-E001, BATCH-0009-E004] The contrary trajectory is materially stronger on democratic resilience. The state of siege remained in force in Nord-Kivu and Ituri, replacing elected civilian governors with military and police officers, suspending elected provincial assemblies, authorizing military courts to prosecute civilians, and being extended more than 50 times without meaningful public debate; Amnesty also reported rights restrictions, harassment and imprisonment of journalists, detention of critics, and failure to meet the ICC notification requirement. [BATCH-0012-R03-E003, BATCH-0012-R03-E004, BATCH-0012-R03-E007] Electoral reform was minimally implemented after 2018, CENI and the Constitutional Court remained perceived as politicized, and the 2023 election combined competition and inclusive party registration with incomplete voter-register auditing, logistical and transparency failures, restricted observation of tabulation, violence, administrative-resource abuse, underrepresentation, disenfranchisement in conflict areas, and historically low turnout. [BATCH-0013-E010, BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E014, BATCH-0028-E018, BATCH-0001-E012, BATCH-0001-E014] Civic and media space also narrowed: journalists, activists, critics, and opposition actors faced arrests, threats, attacks, politically motivated prosecution, excessive force, and a state broadcaster lacking independence; accountability for serious abuses and transitional justice remained incomplete, while the justice system was described as dysfunctional and subject to political and military interference. [BATCH-0025-E008, BATCH-0028-E014, BATCH-0028-E015, BATCH-0028-E017, BATCH-0028-E018, BATCH-0010-E016] A reported 12% fall in documented human-rights violations is qualifying evidence, but it measures reported incidents rather than democratic resilience and may reflect conflict and reporting conditions. [BATCH-0025-E009] Attribution is mixed: Tshisekedi is directly linked to the state-of-siege framework, repeated extensions, appointments, and formal commitments, while many election, security, media, and conflict outcomes concern collective government institutions, security forces, political parties, armed groups, or wartime conditions and do not prove a personal presidential order. The inherited baseline and counterfactual are not sufficiently established, and durability beyond 2023 is unproven. Overall, formal capacity-building and some permitted participation did not amount to demonstrated, independently reviewable, corrected, and durable strengthening of freedom or democratic resilience.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0011-E014","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0001-E012","BATCH-0025-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0012-R03-E004","BATCH-0012-R03-E007","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0028-E014","BATCH-0028-E015","BATCH-0010-E016","BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0025-E008"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied record does not establish a reliable counterfactual against inherited political freedom or democratic resilience.","No supplied evidence demonstrates durable effects beyond the target period.","Formal laws, staffing, audits, monitoring, directives, and ICC cooperation do not by themselves prove independent reviewability, nationwide implementation, correction, or effective remedies.","The CENI audit and some government accounts are institutionally interested; the audit also relied partly on CENI's internal audit.","Many adverse findings concern collective state institutions, security forces, political parties, armed groups, or conflict conditions and do not prove Tshisekedi personally directed each act.","The decline in documented violations may reflect reporting coverage and conflict conditions rather than improved democratic resilience.","The evidence on peaceful transfer, long-term institutional restraint, and corrective institutional response remains incomplete."],"corrections_made":["Added the omitted National Commission on Human Rights monitoring capacity, permitted monitoring, presidential anti-exclusion and anti-fraud directive, and the evidence that prior electoral reforms were minimally implemented and CENI and the Constitutional Court remained perceived as politicized.","Reweighted the synthesis so formal laws, audit, justice, ICC cooperation, and isolated peaceful-protest evidence are treated as limited positive capacity or commitment evidence rather than proof of durable trajectory improvement.","Preserved the distinction between formal institutional activity and independently reviewable, implemented, corrected, and durable democratic resilience.","Retained attribution limits for collective institutional, security, electoral, armed-group, and conflict-related outcomes.","Kept the 12% decline in documented violations as qualifying but non-dispositive evidence."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review would be useful if evidence of inherited baseline conditions, post-2023 durability, actual remedies, or independent institutional corrections becomes available.","The question remains sensitive to the unresolved counterfactual and to the division between presidential responsibility and collective or wartime conditions."]}
